progression.label: Class track
progression.description: The PHB presents paladin as a fighter subclass with its own advancement. The separate UA revision changes its subclass relationship.

progression.label: Class track
progression.description: The PHB presents ranger as a fighter subclass with its own advancement. Race and class-combination restrictions are checked separately.

progression.description: A guide to magic-user XP and level progression. Race, alignment, and class-combination restrictions are checked separately.

progression.label: Class track
progression.description: The magic-user subclass uses its own illusionist advancement table. Race and class-combination restrictions are checked separately.

progression.label: Class track
progression.description: A guide to ordinary thief XP and level progression. The later thief-acrobat specialist path is presented separately.

progression.label: Class track
progression.description: The thief subclass uses its own assassin advancement and guild-rank rules. Race and class-combination restrictions are checked separately.

progression.label: Class track
progression.description: A guide to the monk class’s own advancement and restricted higher ranks. The existing guide’s source conflicts and qualification gaps still apply.

progression.label: Special sequential progression
progression.description: Fighter → thief → bard under Appendix II’s own rules. The supplemental class requires DM acceptance and a human or half-elf with Strength, Wisdom, Dexterity, and Charisma 15+, Intelligence 12+, and Constitution 10+. Change from fighter after reaching level 5 and before level 8; the thief-stage transition is worded “between 5th and 9th.” Bard XP is counted separately, with earlier abilities retained as specified.

progression.label: Class track
progression.description: A guide to cavalier advancement. Social station or sponsorship can require Horseman and Lancer zero-level stages before first-level cavalier abilities; these are stages of this class track.

progression.label: Class track
progression.description: The UA fighter subclass uses its own barbarian advancement. Its class restrictions remain in force; the Class track label makes no separate eligibility ruling.

progression.label: Thief specialist path
progression.description: After five ordinary thief levels, a character with Strength 15+ and Dexterity 16+ may specialize on qualifying for level 6. Training takes six weeks with a thief-acrobat of at least level 10. UA calls this a “split-class” specialist and otherwise treats it as a thief except for the stated changes; it has its own specialist advancement table.

progression.label: UA subclass revision
progression.description: UA makes paladin a cavalier subclass. PHB paladin powers and level advancement remain, with added cavalier abilities and revised entry requirements. This is a revised paladin guide, rather than a simultaneous paladin/cavalier class combination.

progression.label: Advanced XP reset track
progression.description: Continues the druid class through Grand Druid and Hierophant. After reaching at least 3,500,001 XP, a Grand Druid who finds a successor may abdicate and enter the level-16 Hierophant category with XP reset to 1. The reset begins a separate advancement scale within this druid progression.

explainer.title: Class tracks, combinations, and special paths
explainer.description: These labels describe the progression represented by each guide. Check race, abilities, alignment, and campaign requirements in the cited rules before choosing a character’s classes.

sections.label: Concurrent multiclass
sections.description: PHB pp. 32–33 presents combinations operated at the same time by non-human or semi-human characters. The combinations available depend on race; this is a separate procedure from changing professions.

sections.label: Sequential class change (dual-class)
sections.description: PHB p. 33’s human-only profession change stops advancement in the former class. It requires principal attribute scores of at least 15 in the original class and 17 or 18 in the new class, with alignment restrictions. The character retains earlier hit points but begins the new class’s other functions at level 1. Former-class functions restrict new-class XP until the new level exceeds the old one.

sections.label: Special published progressions
sections.description: The bard appendix supplies a fighter → thief → bard sequence. UA supplies a thief-acrobat specialist path and an advanced druid track with an XP reset. Each follows its own cited transition rules; their labels do not grant general permission to combine classes.

terminologyNotes: “Dual-class” is a navigation gloss here. PHB p. 33 heads its sequential rule “The Character With Two Classes.”

The bard appendix permits humans and half-elves, while the general two-class rule requires a human. The bard guide is classified by its appendix sequence rather than automatically assigned that general procedure.
For the bard’s thief-stage transition, PHB p. 117 says “between 5th and 9th.” This metadata retains that wording without resolving its boundary convention.
UA p. 23 calls thief-acrobat a “split-class” specialist; UA p. 25 otherwise treats the specialist as a thief except for the stated changes.
A Class track badge identifies one guide’s advancement table; it makes no finding about eligibility for a permitted race-based class combination.
